$comment: Starter manifest for the docs-shell pattern. Every non-obvious choice has an inline $comment field. `$comment` is not consumed by the shell; it exists as a JSON-native way to embed inline docs. Delete these comments once you understand the schema. Full field-by-field reference: docs/shell/README.md § Manifest schema.

brand.$comment: Brand slot on line 1 of the two-line topnav. `label` appears as text; `href` is where a click on the brand goes (typically your top-level README or index.html). The starter's index.html also has a commented-out line — uncomment it and drop your own SVG at assets/.svg to add a brand icon alongside the label.
brand.label: My Project

theme.$comment: Optional. Delete this whole block to fall back to the shell's built-in GitHub Primer defaults (blue accent, neutral grays, light+dark modes). Every CSS custom property listed in index.html's :root block is overridable — this starter shows the full palette so you can see everything you can tune. To pick just an accent, delete the vars you don't care about. Value guard: only hex / rgb / hsl / named colors pass; anything else is silently dropped. See docs/shell/README.md § Theme system for the complete override list.

$comment_areas: AREAS ARCHITECTURE — the top-level `areas[]` array drives the two-line topnav (line 1 = area buttons, line 2 = docs of the active area). This starter ships a single area with a single doc for the smallest working shell. Add more areas for multi-area navigation.

areas.$comment: One area. `id` is the URL slug for ?area=<id>. `label` is the button text on line 1. `folder` is cosmetic (source paths in each doc's sources[] are relative to this manifest.json, not to `folder`). `defaultDoc` is the doc that loads when ?doc= is absent from the URL. `docs[]` is a non-empty list of doc definitions.
areas.label: Docs

docs.$comment: One doc. `id` is the URL slug for ?doc=<id>. `label` is the button text on line 2. Optional `icon` is a single emoji shown in the sticky page-title header at 22px; empty/absent collapses via CSS `:empty` so the title stays flush. `title` is both the browser <title> and the big page title. Optional `verified` is a provenance line under the title (e.g. 'Updated 2026-07-28'). Optional `sourceLink` puts a chip in the header linking back to the source .md.
docs.label: About
docs.title: About My Project

hero.$comment: HERO BLOCK — sits between the sticky page-title header and the body content. `eyebrow` is a small uppercase pill above the title (chapter numbers, breadcrumbs, status tags). `title` is the big display heading, often mirrors doc.title but can be shorter. `subtitle` is the Big Idea (one-sentence thesis authored per the big-idea skill — https://github.com/fabioc-aloha/Alex_ACT_Steward/blob/main/.github/skills/big-idea/SKILL.md). `description` is optional metadata (provenance, cross-refs, methodology notes) that IS preserved in the manifest but NOT rendered by default since 2026-07-28 — the Big Idea in subtitle carries the summary duty. Uncomment the description-render line in renderHero() to re-enable rendering.
hero.title: About My Project
hero.subtitle: A one-line elevator pitch that appears under the hero title as the Big Idea.
hero.description: Optional metadata paragraph. Preserved in the manifest, not rendered by default.

docs.$comment: OPTIONAL SECOND DOC: HTML-source doc. When every entry in sources[] ends in .html, the shell links directly to the file instead of injecting into the shell wrapper. The topnav button still appears on line 2; clicking it loads the standalone HTML page. Useful for Flint chart reports, exported dashboards, or any pre-built HTML that owns its own cover / hero / typography. See docs/shell/README.md § HTML-source docs. Delete this exemplar if you don't need it.
docs.label: Example report
docs.title: Example Report

areas.$comment_docs_after: TO ADD ANOTHER DOC: append another object to this `docs[]` array. Each new object becomes a button on line 2 of the topnav when this area is active. Minimum required fields per doc: id, label, title, sources[]. Everything else (icon, verified, sourceLink, hero) is optional.

quickJumps.$comment: OPTIONAL PER-AREA QUICKJUMPS — heading-jump shortcuts. The starter's index.html renders these in the topnav-jumps slot on the right of line 1. Some root shell implementations (e.g., Alex_ACT_Steward) do NOT render quickJumps (keeping line 1 minimal); adopters who want them get them by default in the starter. Two shapes below.
quickJumps.$comment_shape: SHAPE 1 — internal heading jump. `label` is the button text. `doc` is the id of an entry in this area's docs[]. `match` is a case-insensitive startsWith prefix that matches any H1/H2/H3 in that doc; the first match wins.
quickJumps.label: Example section

quickJumps.$comment: SHAPE 2 — external cross-shell link. `label` is the button text. `external` is a path relative to this shell's index.html (or an absolute URL). Convention: '→' arrow on outbound siblings, '←' on back-to-root. Delete this exemplar if you have no sibling shell to link to.
quickJumps.label: Sibling shell →
